chunks: And my father narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdillah ibn Al-Mughirah, from Al-Abbas ibn Amir, who said: Yūsuf Al-Anbāri informed me from Qā'id Al-Ḥannāṭ

He said: I said to Abi Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'They go to the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) with the wailers and food.' He said, 'I have heard.' Then he said, 'O Qā'id! Whoever goes to the grave of Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) knowing his rights, his past and future sins will be forgiven.'

key_terms.النَّوَائِحِ: Wailers or those who lament, often referring to professional mourners or groups reciting elegies.
key_terms.ذَنْبِهِ: His sin, referring to the sins of the visitor.
key_terms.عَارِفاً بِحَقِّهِ: Knowing his rights, implying deep spiritual and theological recognition of the Imam's status.
key_terms.قَائِدٌ الْحَنَّاطُ: Qā'id Al-Ḥannāṭ, a narrator in the chain.
key_terms.قَبْرَ الْحُسَيْنِ: The grave of Al-Husayn ibn Ali, a central site for Shia pilgrimage.

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam Al-Husayn with knowledge of his rights?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* underscores the concept of *‘irfan* (gnostic recognition) as the key condition for the comprehensive forgiveness of sins during the Ziyārah of Imām al-Ḥusayn (a.s.). It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis that mere physical presence is insufficient; rather, one must acknowledge the specific spiritual and theological rights (*huquq*) of the Ahl al-Bayt to attain this divine mercy.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 8. My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Mughīrah, from ‘Abbās ibn ‘Āmir, from Yūsuf Al-Anbāri, from Qā`id Al-Ḥannāť, who said:

I said to Abil Ḥasan (Imam Kāżim (a.s.)), “Some people go to (the Ziyārah of) the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) and they take people to lament and (they also take) food with them.” Imam (a.s.) said, “I have heard this. O Qā`id! Those who go to (the Ziyārah of) the grave of Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.) knowing his rights will be forgiven for all of their past and future sins.”
